name: Svinoriz 10 Opto
about: The Svinoriz 10 Opto's component spec (DRN-03; p5-drone task 1.2), written from docs/object-sheets/drone.md, letter T's frame, arms, packs and legs (D-043) and the pilot's simpler drone (D-050): the fiber coil beneath the frame, fore-aft between the two packs, which run along the sides below the arms; a plain plastic bottle strapped rigidly on top, fore-aft, the only load, its filled mass the setup's additional weight; four carbon tube legs on two fore-aft skids. legs_off is the legs-off build: legs, T-joints and skids off and every other part where it is; the drone lifts off the upside-down chair's posts under its arms, so the coil never touches the ground. The parts stand at the nominal in-flight loadout, a 1.0 kg bottle and the coil half paid out, 4.83 kg. Body frame of DetMath.cs: x right, y up, z forward, metres from the arm-plane centre. Nothing is balanced: the stack's forward offset puts the centre of mass about 0.5 mm forward (derived) and leaves a small product of inertia I_yz, and the mass build keeps both. Every number is labelled where it stands (pilot, measured, published, derived or assumed) and the note gives its source or its calculation; 'the sheet' is the object sheet, 'T' the reference letter.

fields.labelled number: {"value": <number, or [x, y, z], or a list>, "label": "pilot" | "measured" | "published" | "derived" | "assumed", "note": "<source or calculation>"}; the note is optional, the label is not
fields.bootstrap: true for p6-flight-core's stand-in (now a test fixture); this researched file sets false
fields.parts: every rigid part the mass build sums (PHB-02): name (unique), kind (box | cylinder), material (carbon | aluminium | steel | polymer | li_ion | electronics), mass_kg (above 0), position_m (the part's centre); a box has size_m, its extents along body x, y, z; a cylinder is solid, with diameter_m, length_m and axis (the direction of its length, normalised when read). A part is a mass shape: its inertia, not its look (the props and arms say how they map)
fields.motors: four, in Betaflight's Quad X order (rear right, front right, rear left, front left): position_m (the prop hub, where the thrust acts), spin (cw | ccw seen from above; cw is a positive rotation about body +y), kv_rpm_per_v, resistance_ohm (the DC model's resistance: winding, ESC and leads), no_load_current_a (the bearings' and iron's loss, as the torque Kt·I0), rotor_inertia_kg_m2 (bell, shaft and prop about the shaft), magnet_poles, esc_tau_s (the ESC's command lag: the DShot frame, the PWM and the winding's L/R as one first-order lag), esc_current_limit_a (the ESC's current limit: the motor's current never passes it while the ESC drives); the motor's lag τ_m = J/(Kt·Ke/R + ∂Q/∂ω) follows from these and the load
fields.props: the four props, alike: diameter_m, blades, pitch_m (geometric, per revolution), k_t_n_per_rad2_s2 (T = k_T·n², n in rad/s) and kappa_m (Q = κ·T), both static at reference_rpm (one of static_rpm's points); static_rpm with static_thrust_ratio and static_torque_ratio (C_T and C_P there over their values at reference_rpm: the coefficients' change with rpm); inflow_advance_ratio (J = V_a/(n·D) of the axial inflow, from 0) with inflow_thrust_ratio and inflow_torque_ratio (C_T and C_P there over their static values); linear between points, held at the ends; h_force_n_per_m_s (the rotor's in-plane drag, the H-force, per m/s of its hub's in-plane airspeed at reference_rpm, growing in proportion to the rotor's speed)
fields.packs: two (PHB-03): part (the pack's mass part), series and parallel cells, cell_capacity_ah, r_cell_ohm, ocv_v (one cell's open-circuit voltage at states of charge 0, 1/(n−1), …, 1)
fields.legs: parts (the four leg parts, in Betaflight's corner order; a leg's length is its part's, its foot the part's lower end, where it meets level ground), stiffness_n_per_m and damping_n_s_per_m (each leg's own spring and damper, in series with the ground), foot_radius_m (the foot's curvature); legs off is legs_off's build
fields.legs_off: the legs-off build (D-043, D-050): removed (every part that comes off with the legs, the four leg parts among them; they weigh 0 kg), moved ({part name: its labelled centre on the legs-off build}; D-050's layout moves none: the coil is beneath and the bottle on top on both builds); every other part stays as it is
fields.coil: part (the spool's mass part, whose mass falls as the line pays out), spool_mass_kg (empty, with its housing), fiber_mass_kg and fiber_length_m (the line on a full spool); the part's mass here is this file's loadout
fields.payload: part (the payload's mass part, set to the pilot's payload: D-050's plain plastic bottle strapped rigidly on top, its filled mass the setting), mass_min_kg and mass_max_kg (the setting's range, APP-03); the part is the bottle at its mass here, this file's loadout; another payload scales it uniformly by the cube root of the mass ratio, growing away from the arm plane (its face toward the frame stays put), and 0 kg leaves it off
fields.stand: the legs-off launch stand (D-022, D-043): material, post_radius_m (each post on a motor diagonal, from the stand's centre), post_height_m (the post tops above the ground), post_diameter_m, mass_kg
fields.aero: the airframe's drag (p6-flight-core 1.5): air_density_kg_m3; body_area_m2 (the silhouette less the coil's, projected along body x, y and z: side, top, front); body_center_of_pressure_m (where the body's drag acts); drag_coefficient (of the body's silhouette and of the coil, whose own drag acts at the coil part's centre with its cylinder's silhouette)
fields.contacts: the contact model (p6-flight-core 1.6): margin_m (StaticContacts' margin), crash_accel_m_s2 and crash_prop_speed_m_s (the crash thresholds), impact_window_s and impact_speed_m_s (what an impact is), friction_stiffness_ratio, damping_mass_share, ground_friction_static and ground_friction_kinetic, ring_segments; shapes[]: name (unique), part (the mass part it belongs to: a part at 0 kg has no shapes, and a moved or scaled part moves or scales its shapes), role (support: a load-bearing sphere on a skid, on the ground and on objects, carried by its corner's leg spring; skid: a skid segment's capsule, on objects only, a contact within two radii of a touching support of its part dropped as the same support; body: a frame part on the ground and on objects, with its own stiffness_n_per_m (across body y), stiffness_up_n_per_m (along it; the same when absent) and damping_ratio; disc: a prop disc at its motor's hub, radius_m the flown prop's, half_thickness_m the blade's, strikes only), corner (rr | fr | rl | fl, for supports, skids and discs), material (carbon_composite | polymer | aluminium: the drone side of the contact), a_m (a sphere's centre or a capsule's core end), b_m (a capsule's other core end), radius_m

kv_rpm_per_v.label: published
kv_rpm_per_v.note: 3115 900 KV (Surpass Hobby Bat S3115, K§5.1; Flash Hobby Arthur, rated 3–6S)

resistance_ohm.label: derived
resistance_ohm.note: the Flash Hobby Arthur 3115 900 KV bench on 6S (published, flyingtech.co.uk, its FH1050 rows): (d·V − Ke·ω)/(I/d) = 0.106 Ω at 50 % (25.12 V, 9027 rpm, 11.93 A), 0.107 at 70 %, 0.110 at 80 %, 0.127 at 100 % (24.62 V, 14 691 rpm, 65.26 A); 0.11, a warm winding through the hover-to-cruise range: the winding's own 0.046 Ω (published) plus the ESC, the leads and heat. At full throttle the model then turns about 4 % fast against the 100 % row

no_load_current_a.label: assumed
no_load_current_a.note: a 3115-class 900 KV motor's idle current, about 1 A at 10 V; not published for these motors. Its torque Kt·I0, 0.011 N·m, is 6 % of the hover drag torque

rotor_inertia_kg_m2.label: derived
rotor_inertia_kg_m2.note: ±30 %: the 16 g prop about 4.7e-5 (UMN's measured APC 12x3.8SF with its motor and adaptor, 1.12e-4, scaled by m·D² to 16 g and 10 inches; a uniform rod would be 8.6e-5) plus the bell, about 35 g of magnets and can at 17 mm, 1.2e-5. With R and the prop's load it makes τ_m about 40 ms at hover (design 5's 40–60 ms)

magnet_poles.label: published
magnet_poles.note: 12N14P (Flash Hobby Arthur 3115, the sheet's research table): 7 pole pairs

esc_tau_s.label: derived
esc_tau_s.note: p7b-airframe 1.0: the command's way from the flight controller to the motor's torque as one first-order lag, the sum of its delays (their first moment: within 0.1° of their phase below 60 Hz). The DShot300 frame, 53 µs (published: 16 bits at 300 kbit/s, sent every 250 µs, fc-profiles §1); the ESC takes the duty up at once (published sources: Bluejay sets its PWM registers in the frame's interrupt, AM32 in its 20 kHz loop, within 50 µs); the 24 kHz PWM's next period and its mean, about 42 µs (AM32's nominal 24 kHz, its source): about 0.1 ms in all (derived). Then the winding's current rise L/R, 0.3 ms (assumed, 0.1–0.6 ms: no inductance is published for these motors). The duty is not slewed: BLHeli_32's Maximum Acceleration (0.1–25.5 %/ms or maximum, its manual) is left at maximum, no limit, as ESC vendors advise; Bluejay has none (its source); AM32's ramp (16 %/ms above 40 k erpm, 6 below, 2 at start: its source) moves the filtered 200 °/s step by under 0.1 point and is left out. Design 5's 5 ms (assumed) gave that step 40.9 % overshoot (roll) against 29.2 % here; 0.2–0.7 ms gives 28.7–30.0 %

esc_current_limit_a.label: assumed
esc_current_limit_a.note: the policy (p6-flight-core 1.5): the motor's published 40 A maximum (Surpass Hobby Bat S3115 900 KV, K§5.1; K§5.3's realistic maximum current) set as the ESC's current protection, which BLHeli_32 applies per ESC and fast enough to hold the current during accelerations too (its manual); AM32's limit is optional and Bluejay or BLHeli_S ESCs sense no current. Without it the model's motor draws 47.5 A at full duty on a full pack and 115 A in a spin-up from idle to full; with it the full-duty thrust falls from 14.24 to 11.93 kgf (K§5.3: 9.0–12.5), the yaw acceleration over full yaw's first 50 ms from hover from about 1650 to 1290 °/s² and the steady yaw authority from 796 to 745 °/s²; hover and liftoff draw far less and are untouched. A higher value models an ESC without a limit (G7 asks the pilot how the yaw kick feels)

diameter_m.label: measured
diameter_m.note: 10 inches: T measures 10.0–10.4 tip to tip at the 452 mm scale, the class's 10-inch (K§5.1)

pitch_m.label: assumed
pitch_m.note: 4.5 inches: the prop whose published table gives k_T and κ, inside the sheet's 10 × 4.5–5 class

k_t_n_per_rad2_s2.label: derived
k_t_n_per_rad2_s2.note: APC 10x4.5MR, 2-blade, its published static performance data (apcprop.com, PER3_10x45MR.dat, v2022-0915): 12.43 N at 9000 rpm, C_T 0.1079–0.1097 over 8000–12 000 rpm, so k_T = T/n² = 1.394–1.418e-5 there, 1.400e-5 at 9000 rpm, the hover (8800–9100 rpm at 4.8–5.2 kg). The table is APC's computation; the Flash Hobby 3115 900 KV bench (published) gives 1.55–1.69e-5 with its own 10 × 5 of unstated blade count, and UIUC's measured static C_T of 2-blade 10-inch APC props is 0.091–0.130 below 6700 rpm (m-selig.ae.illinois.edu)

kappa_m.label: derived
kappa_m.note: the same table's static torque over thrust: 0.01454 at 8000, 0.01443 at 9000 and 0.01436 m at 10 000 rpm (C_P 0.0387, κ = C_P·D/(2π·C_T)); below design 5's assumed 0.015–0.02, which was for a 3-blade: a 4.5-inch 2-blade turns less torque per newton, so yaw authority is a little weaker

reference_rpm.label: derived
reference_rpm.note: k_T and κ are the table's static values at 9000 rpm, the hover of 4.8–5.2 kg

static_rpm.label: published
static_rpm.note: the APC 10x4.5MR table's static rows (PER3_10x45MR.dat, v2022-0915)

static_thrust_ratio.label: derived
static_thrust_ratio.note: C_T over its 0.1083 at 9000 rpm: C_T rises from 0.106 at 1000 to 0.111 at 14 000 rpm (the blades' Reynolds number), which a constant k_T leaves out

static_torque_ratio.label: derived
static_torque_ratio.note: C_P over its 0.0387 at 9000 rpm: the drag torque per n² is 23 % higher at 1000 rpm (idle), 1–3 % between 6000 and 17 000

inflow_advance_ratio.label: published
inflow_advance_ratio.note: the same table at 9000 rpm, every second row to zero thrust at J 0.588 (linear between them within 0.06 % of C_T and 0.26 % of C_P)

inflow_thrust_ratio.label: derived
inflow_thrust_ratio.note: C_T(J) over the static C_T at 9000 rpm: APC's blade-element and momentum computation of the axial-inflow derate (PHB-03); the same ratios hold within 0.5 % from 4000 to 18 000 rpm

inflow_torque_ratio.label: derived
inflow_torque_ratio.note: C_P(J) over the static C_P at 9000 rpm: the torque falls more slowly than the thrust, so the inflow costs power as momentum theory says (within 2 % to J 0.3 from 4000 to 18 000 rpm, 5 % by J 0.5)

h_force_n_per_m_s.label: assumed
h_force_n_per_m_s.note: tuned (design 6) so the model flies clip P's measured 22.7° of pitch at wind.md §5.3's nominal 13 m/s of cruise (22.8° at 0.225), where wind.md derives its 1.8° of lean per m/s of crosswind: the model then needs 1.9° per m/s there and 1.27° per m/s in a hover (design 6's 0.95–2.6). That is 0.18 s⁻¹ of linear rotor drag per unit mass at the hover's 8800 rpm, inside the 0.1–0.4 s⁻¹ reported for small quadrotors (wind.md §5.3). The pilot's cruise answer (K§8.2) points to less drag still: here 17 m/s takes 33.6° of pitch; p7c-wind settles it with T0

series.label: derived
series.note: 6S: the 3115 900 KV motors are rated 3–6S (published); the class's 8S (fc-profiles.md) would need about 900·6/8 = 675 KV, and at 8S these motors would draw about 80 A each at full throttle on this prop, twice their 40 A (derived)

parallel.label: derived
parallel.note: two identical packs (T, the pilot's 'a couple of batteries') in parallel make the pilot's 6S4P (pilot: 6S4P to 6S5P, 20–35 Ah): 20 Ah, 432 Wh, the one even arrangement inside 4P–5P; T's packs, two cells high and 0.22 m long, hold 12 cells each

cell_capacity_ah.label: published
cell_capacity_ah.note: Molicel INR21700-P50B: 5.0 Ah typical, 4.85 Ah minimum, 3.6 V, 2.5 V cut-off, 60 A continuous, 71 ± 1 g, Ø21.45 × 70.05 mm (akkuteile.de). 5 Ah makes 6S4P the pilot's 20 Ah (a 4.5 Ah P45B gives 18), and its 60 A covers the about 50 A a cell at full throttle in 4P (derived), which a 25 A Samsung 50S does not

r_cell_ohm.label: assumed
r_cell_ohm.note: under load, 1.5 × the P50B's published ≤ 8 mΩ at shipping (AC); the sheet's 12–16 mΩ, K§5.3's 15 mΩ; 1.4's sag scenario checks it

ocv_v.label: assumed
ocv_v.note: one cell at state of charge 0, 0.05, …, 1, over the P50B's published 5.0 Ah from its 4.2 V charge to its 2.5 V cut-off (published, akkuteile.de): the shape of the P50B's and like 5 Ah 21700 NMC cells' published low-rate discharge curves, read by shape and not digitised, so assumed; 3.40–4.07 V over 10–90 % (K§5.3: 3.4–4.1 V), the knee below 10 %: 4 V a unit of charge from 10 to 5 %, 14 V from 5 % to the cut-off (p7b-airframe 1.5; model 11's table stopped at 3.0 V, so the pack never emptied)

stiffness_n_per_m.label: assumed
stiffness_n_per_m.note: the vertical give of the plastic clamps, T-joints and skid overhangs, 5–20 kN/m a leg (the sheet), its middle; the tube itself bends sideways at about 6.6 kN/m (derived, the sheet); kept by 1.6's bounce scenario on a rigid floor: down at 0.50 m/s with the sticks held it leaves again at 0.28 m/s (0.56 of the touch) and rises 0.21 m, with the throttle cut it hops 3 mm and rests 0.28 s after the touch (the manifesto's §2.6; soil's loss is 7a's)

damping_n_s_per_m.label: derived
damping_n_s_per_m.note: ζ 0.2 (the sheet's 0.1–0.3, assumed) on a quarter of the 5.18 kg take-off mass: c = 2ζ·√(k·m) = 45 N·s/m; kept by 1.6's bounce scenario (see stiffness_n_per_m)

foot_radius_m.label: measured
foot_radius_m.note: the skid tube's radius (T: Ø9–10 mm); the feet are skids, so each leg's foot is its T-joint on the skid

spool_mass_kg.label: derived
spool_mass_kg.note: the housing and cradle: the pilot's 1.0 kg coil less its 0.69 kg of line (a retail 10 km canister is 0.95 kg with its fiber, published; the sheet)

fiber_mass_kg.label: derived
fiber_mass_kg.note: 10 km of 0.069 kg/km: glass Ø125 µm at 2.2 g/cm³ plus its coating to Ø250 µm at about 1.15 g/cm³ (assumed; the sheet)

fiber_length_m.label: published
fiber_length_m.note: the class's 10 km spools (K§5.1), the pilot's about 1 kg

mass_min_kg.label: assumed
mass_min_kg.note: the setup's range starts with no payload (APP-03)

mass_max_kg.label: published
mass_max_kg.note: OTU-10's payload of up to 2 kg (K§5.1), the setup's top (APP-03)

post_radius_m.label: derived
post_radius_m.note: each post on a motor diagonal, its cap under the arm just inboard of the motor can: 0.226 − 0.0186 − 0.0074 m (the sheet)

post_diameter_m.label: assumed
post_diameter_m.note: a chair's 20 × 20 × 1.5 mm square tube, read as its width (the sheet)

mass_kg.label: derived
mass_kg.note: about 1.8 m of that tube at 0.871 kg/m (111 mm² × 7850 kg/m³, published steel) with its caps and welds (the sheet)

air_density_kg_m3.label: published
air_density_kg_m3.note: ISA sea level, 15 °C: APC's tables and k_T are at it

body_area_m2.label: derived
body_area_m2.note: the sheet's silhouettes (Physics role, ±30 %) for D-043's layout, side 0.056, top 0.07 and front 0.06 m², re-derived for D-050's: less the slung payload's visible 0.008 side (its Ø0.10 m end), 0.005 top (its ends past the packs) and 0.021 front (0.24 × 0.10 m less the legs before it); plus the bottle's 0.019 side (0.26 × 0.08 m less the neck's taper), 0.003 top (its 0.019 less the plates it hides) and 0.005 front (its Ø0.080 m end); the coil beneath hides 0.009 of the packs side-on (0.20 × 0.045 m) and the plates top-on, where it hid them on top. Then less the coil's own, which the coil's drag takes from its part: 0.017 side, 0.017 top (0.083 × 0.20 m) and 0.005 front (its Ø0.083 m end). The bottle's silhouette is the nominal 1 kg one at every payload setting (assumed: ±0.01 m² side between 0 and 2 kg)

body_center_of_pressure_m.label: derived
body_center_of_pressure_m.note: the silhouette's area-weighted centre, from D-043's assumed 0.07 m below the arm plane with the slung payload (y −0.108) replaced by the bottle on top (+0.087) and the packs' share the coil hides (−0.043) taken out: +0.004 m side-on and −0.029 m front-on (derived), one point for every direction between them, on the centreline (±0.02 m); it stays put on the legs-off build (assumed)

drag_coefficient.label: assumed
drag_coefficient.note: a silhouette of rounded bluff parts, the coil's cylinder alike: finite cylinders 0.6–1.0 by their length over diameter, boxes with rounded edges 0.8–1.05 (Hoerner, Fluid-Dynamic Drag); 0.9 × the sheet's 0.06 m² front is wind.md §5.3's nominal C_D·A of 0.05 m²

margin_m.label: derived
margin_m.note: StaticContacts' margin: a latched pair stays in the result while its part is past the shape but inside its plane, so the margin covers the deepest stop less what the part needs to clear the shape (P2): a motor can (2e5 N/m) at the drone's 30 m/s stops in 30·√(4.7/2e5) = 0.146 m and clears a 20 mm tube after 0.057 m. A skid driven that fast into a rod would snap in truth, which is phase 7's breakage; here it logs a tunnel

crash_accel_m_s2.label: assumed
crash_accel_m_s2.note: 50 g of the body from its contacts ends the flight (p6-flight-core design 7); a 0.3 m drop on the legs peaks near 19 g

crash_prop_speed_m_s.label: assumed
crash_prop_speed_m_s.note: a prop disc entering a rigid shape or the ground faster than this along the normal ends the flight (design 7)

impact_window_s.label: assumed
impact_window_s.note: an impact's peak acceleration and impulse are taken over its first 50 ms (K§6.10: a crash is decided in the 50 ms before it)

impact_speed_m_s.label: assumed
impact_speed_m_s.note: a touch closing faster than this starts an impact; a slower one is a resting or sliding touch

friction_stiffness_ratio.label: assumed
friction_stiffness_ratio.note: the stick anchor's tangential stiffness over the normal (K§7.1 step 5, surfaces-review §1)

damping_mass_share.label: assumed
damping_mass_share.note: a shape's damping ratio is taken on a quarter of the take-off mass, as legs.damping_n_s_per_m is: c = 2ζ·√(k·m/4)

ground_friction_static.label: assumed
ground_friction_static.note: the drone on the ground's surfaces, rigid at G7: one pair for every surface, K§7.2's belt_bare (the stub floor's); 7a reads each surface's own

ring_segments.label: derived
ring_segments.note: a 12-gon's chords stay within R·(1 − cos 15°) = 4.3 mm of the 0.127 m rim, about the blade's half-thickness (P4)

a_m.label: measured

b_m.label: measured
